_comment: Illustrative output of `hardening-agent audit --format json` on an Ubuntu 24.04 EC2 instance, trimmed to a representative subset of checks. Generate a real one with: hardening-agent audit --format json -o report.json

results.title: SSH direct root login is disabled
results.rationale: Direct root login removes per-user accountability and gives brute-force attackers a known-valid username. Administrators should log in as themselves and escalate with sudo, which leaves an audit trail.

results.title: root is the only account with UID 0
results.description: No account other than root may have UID 0.
results.rationale: A second UID 0 account is full root access under a name that does not look like root, which is a classic persistence mechanism that survives password rotation and is easy to overlook in an audit.
results.detail: root is the only UID 0 account

results.title: /etc/shadow is not readable by non-root users
results.description: /etc/shadow must be mode 0640 or stricter, owned by root.
results.rationale: /etc/shadow holds password hashes. Any local read gives an attacker an offline cracking target with no rate limit and no logging.

results.title: SSH private host keys are protected
results.description: Private host keys must be mode 0640 or stricter and owned by root.
results.rationale: A leaked private host key allows an attacker to impersonate this server and transparently machine-in-the-middle every SSH session, including the credentials and commands within it.

results.title: Full address space layout randomisation is enabled
results.rationale: ASLR randomises the memory layout of every process, which is the baseline mitigation that makes memory-corruption exploits probabilistic rather than reliable. Value 2 randomises the heap too.

results.title: A host firewall is active with a default-deny inbound policy
results.description: ufw or nftables must be active and default-deny for incoming traffic.
results.rationale: Security groups protect the north-south edge, but a host firewall is what limits east-west movement once an attacker is already inside the VPC. Default-deny means a service accidentally bound to 0.0.0.0 is not automatically reachable.
results.detail: ufw is active with default-deny incoming

results.title: Automatic security updates are enabled
results.description: unattended-upgrades must be installed and active.
results.rationale: The overwhelming majority of real-world compromises exploit a vulnerability with an available patch. Automated security patching closes the window between disclosure and remediation without depending on a human being on call.

results.title: IPv4 forwarding is disabled
results.description: net.ipv4.ip_forward must be 0 on hosts that are not routers.
results.rationale: A host that forwards packets can be used to pivot between network segments, bypassing firewall rules that assume traffic terminates at this machine. Only routers, NAT gateways and container hosts need this enabled.
results.detail: container runtime detected; IPv4 forwarding is required for bridge networking

results.title: Time synchronisation is active
results.description: systemd-timesyncd, chrony or ntpd must be running.
results.rationale: Correlating logs across hosts during an incident requires accurate clocks. Clock drift also breaks TLS certificate validation and time-based authentication such as TOTP and AWS SigV4.

results.title: Password expiry policy is configured
results.description: PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs must be 365 or fewer.
results.rationale: Bounded credential lifetime limits how long a leaked password stays useful. Kept at LOW severity because modern guidance (NIST 800-63B) favours breach-triggered rotation over forced expiry.
